key_insight: Speculative decoding works best when a small draft model predicts tokens similarly to the larger target model. This paper studies draft calibration to close that distribution gap and improve token acceptance.
problem_solved: Differences between draft and target token distributions cause proposed tokens to be rejected, limiting the inference speedup from speculative decoding.
method: Use a lightweight draft model to propose tokens, then verify those proposals in parallel with the target model.
Study draft calibration through the L1 distance between target distribution p and draft distribution q, which is directly related to acceptance probability.
Aim to align draft predictions with target predictions; the supplied abstract is truncated and does not specify the calibration algorithm or results.
impact: Better draft–target alignment could help practitioners accelerate LLM serving by increasing accepted draft tokens and improving inference-time compute utilization. The supplied excerpt provides no quantitative speedup results.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: draft model proposes tokens → target model verifies in parallel → accepted tokens advance generation.
Conceptual before-and-after token probability charts showing draft and target distributions becoming more similar.
Illustrative plot linking smaller L1 distribution gaps to higher token acceptance, clearly labeled as conceptual.
Token strip with accepted proposals in green and rejected proposals in red.
paper_title: Draft Calibration for Speculative Decoding: Accelerating LLM Serving by Matching Draft and Target Distributions
paper_authors: Yuxing Liu, Wei Zuo, Walid Krichene, Tong Zhang, Li Zhang
